---
title: "check-template-identity.yml"
---

Blocking check for a template repository.
It fails a repository made from the template
while that repository's config files still hold the template's own identity.
GitHub's "Use this template" button copies a template's files once,
so a new site starts with the template's site URL, repository URL, and title.
Nothing reports them:
the site renders,
and its "Edit this page" link opens the template's repository.
This implements
[gha#2154](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/2154)
for [qwt#207](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/qwt/issues/207).

The template ships the caller workflow,
so every repository made from it runs the check from its first commit.
A line of a named file is reported when it holds any of these:

- the template's repository URL, `github.com/<owner>/<name>`;
- the template's Pages URL, `<owner>.github.io/<name>`;
- a literal listed in `strings`, such as the template's title.

Matching ignores case.
A match that is part of a longer name on either side,
such as `github.com/<owner>/<name>-fork`, does not count.
The same holds for a listed literal.
A dot with a letter or digit after it carries a name on,
as in `github.com/<owner>/<name>.v2`,
except the `.git` of a clone URL.
A dot that ends a sentence does not.
So a page under the template's site, such as `<owner>.github.io/<name>.html`,
is not reported, while `<owner>.github.io/<name>/` is.
A line that should keep the value, such as a credit link to the template,
passes with `check-template-identity: allow: <reason>` on that line,
for example in a YAML comment.

In the template itself there is nothing to check,
so the job says so and passes.
A fork that keeps the template's name under another owner
is a different repository, so the check runs there.

## Scope

The check reads the named tracked files whole,
because a value the new repository never changed is on no line a diff adds.
It stops with an error when no tracked file matches `files`,
whatever `fail` says,
so a wrong list cannot pass by reading nothing.
It stops the same way, with exit status 2, when a matched file cannot be read.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default           | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | ----------------- | ----------- |
| `template`     | string  | required          | The template repository, as `owner/name`. |
| `files`        | string  | `'_quarto.yml _quarto-website.yml _quarto-book.yml DESCRIPTION index.qmd'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of the tracked files to read. |
| `strings`      | string  | `''`              | Newline-separated extra literals a derived repository must not keep, such as the template's title or placeholder author. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `true`            | Fail the workflow when a file still holds the template's identity. Set `false` for warning annotations only. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`          | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository, because [a public repository's pull requests can run arbitrary code on it](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167). |

The composite action also takes `repository`,
which defaults to the repository the workflow runs in.

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-template-identity.yml in a TEMPLATE repo,
# and set `template` to that repo. "Use this template" copies the workflow
# into every new repository, where it fails until the new repository's config
# no longer holds the template's repository URL, Pages URL, or a listed
# literal. In the template itself it passes with a notice.
# Blocking by default.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check template identity

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-template-identity.yml@v3
    with:
      template: your-org/your-template  # owner/name of the template repo
      # files: '_quarto.yml DESCRIPTION'  # tracked files to read
      # strings: |                        # extra literals, one per line
      #   Your Template's Title
      # fail: true                        # set false to warn only (defaults to true)
```

See
[`examples/check-template-identity.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-template-identity.yml)
for the full caller stub.
